pages.text: Matter squeezed until electrons are pressed into protons: neutron-degenerate matter, held up by the Pauli principle (P = Kρ^(5/3)). The mass and pressure you choose set the density and radius; general relativity sets the limits.
$(thing)Set$(): Mass, Compression pressure, Spin frequency, Seed field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Compressor pressure ripple: p·(1 ± 1%·d).

$(thing)Limits$(): Above the TOV mass: collapse into a black hole; Buchdahl limit exceeded: no static star is possible; Spinning past the mass-shedding limit; Interlock: flux-compression coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the flux-compression coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Compression proceeds at a fixed pace.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Density ρ: ρ = (P/K)^(3/5),  K = (3π²)^(2/3)ħ²/(5m_n^(8/3))$(br)Density: log₁₀ ρ$(br)Radius: R = (3M/4πρ)^(1/3)$(br)Schwarzschild radius: r_s = 2GM/c²$(br)Compactness: C = r_s/R$(br)Surface redshift: z = (1 − r_s/R)^(−½) − 1$(br)Mass-shedding frequency: f_K = √(GM/R³)/2π
